Q: Beginner friendly tech stack for a mobile app development? A:

There are packages that you can use to work with MariaDB, for example, but there are many more that allow you to use also the cloud infrastructures provided by Amazon, Google and so on.
You could also point out that it's actually not limited to Android and iOS: you can develop also for desktop OSes, all of them, and web platforms by writing the same code once for all of them (package compatibility aside). Well, yeah, you should probably have a different GUI between mobile and desktop versions, but that is something you can worry later.

Q: How to map a C function to Java Native Method using JavaCpp A:

There are no problems to use JavaCPP for building a bridge for C library. All C functions will be placed in one global Java class.

Q: CollectionView and BindableLayout are treated as comparable, but don't seem to be? A:

Vertical and Horizontal - are more performant, in situations where you know you do not want to change it dynamically - always specify it.

When you need dynamic - use the Orientation bindable property.

CollectionView - besides all other benefits (of templating for example, pull to refresh, swipe, remaining items for lazy loading, etc), it also makes your program performant, by making it calculate and render only immediately needed items. To the point it is not even questionable if you can replace it or not.

A BindableLayout is exactly what the names suggest - a picker from list of layouts that allow you to determine how they look at runtime.

If your goal is to place 3 labels one under the other, you can in fact achieve this picking any path, and you will probably notice no difference for that use case.

The reality is that each of those use cases will matter, if you want to modify how those 3 labels are arranged, how they will look like during runtime, and will your application will even be useful when they are 3000.

Q: Issues duplicating across columns A:

For the cell A2, if A2 is equal to any of B2:C, can be expressed as custom formula:

=ARRAYFORMULA(OR($A2=$B$2:$C))

Now apply the same formula to

A2:A

in the conditional formatting rule.

Q: gnuplot - plot random points inside an ellipse A:

Based on @Bernhard's answer, here is how you can do that with gnuplot only. To reuse a random number, you can put the two rand calls and the assignments to variables in the first argument of the using statement, separated by commas. The using statements are evaluated from left to right, so you can access those variables in all following using parameters.

To demonstrate this, see the following examples:

set samples 1000
plot '+' using (x=rand(0), y=rand(0), x):(y)

Applying this to the ellipsoid, this gives the script:

a=3
b=2
phi=30*pi/180

max(x,y) = (x > y ? x : y)
set xrange[-max(a,b):max(a,b)]
set yrange[-max(a,b):max(a,b)]

set offset 0.1,0.1,0.1,0.1
set samples 2000

ex(x, y) = a*(2*x-1)
ey(x, y) = b*(sqrt(1-((2*x-1))**2))*(2*y-1)

unset key    
plot '+' using (x=rand(0), y=rand(0), ex(x,y)*cos(phi)-ey(x,y)*sin(phi)):\
               (ey(x,y)*cos(phi)+ex(x,y)*sin(phi)) pt 7 ps 0.5

with the result:

This, however, leads to an apparently unequal distribution of the points (see the agglomarations at the ellipse's ends, see @andyras's comment). To avoid this, here is how you can filter equally distributed random points to be inside the ellipsoid:

a=3
b=2
set angles degree
phi=30

max(x,y) = (x > y ? x : y)
set xrange[-max(a,b):max(a,b)]
set yrange[-max(a,b):max(a,b)]

set offset 0.1,0.1,0.1,0.1
set samples 2000
set size ratio 1

check(x, y) = (((x/a)**2 + (y/b)**2) <= 1)
unset key
plot '+' using (x=2*a*(rand(0)-0.5), y=2*b*(rand(0)-0.5), \
     check(x,y) ? x*cos(phi)-y*sin(phi) : 1/0):\
     (x*sin(phi)+y*cos(phi)) pt 7 ps 0.5

This gives the much better result:

Extending this to three dimensions:

a=3
b=1
c=1
set angles degree
phi=30

mx(x,y) = (x > y ? x : y)
max(x,y,z) = mx(mx(x,y), mx(x,z))
set xrange[-max(a,b,c):max(a,b,c)]
set yrange[-max(a,b,c):max(a,b,c)]
set zrange[-max(a,b,c):max(a,b,c)]

set offset 0.1,0.1,0.1,0.1
set samples 2000
set size ratio 1

set ticslevel 0
set view 60, 330

check(x, y, z) = (((x/a)**2 + (y/b)**2 + (z/c)**2) <= 1)
unset key
splot '+' using (x = 2*a*(rand(0)-0.5), \
                 y = 2*b*(rand(0)-0.5), \
                 z=2*c*(rand(0)-0.5), \
                 check(x,y,z) ? x*cos(phi)-y*sin(phi) : 1/0):\
                 (x*sin(phi)+y*cos(phi)):(z) pt 7 ps 0.5

with the result:
